headword: {春夏秋冬|しゅんかしゅうとう}
gloss: the four seasons; spring, summer, autumn, and winter

definitions.gloss: the four seasons; spring, summer, autumn, and winter
definitions.explanation: A literary and formal way to refer to all four seasons as a group. Used to express the full cycle of the year and seasonal changes.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{春夏秋冬|しゅんかしゅうとう}がある。
{春夏秋冬|しゅんかしゅうとう}、それぞれの{季節|きせつ}に{楽|たの}しみがある。
examples.english: Each of the four seasons has its own pleasures.

examples.japanese: この{庭園|ていえん}は{春夏秋冬|しゅんかしゅうとう}を{通|つう}じて{美|うつく}しい{景色|けしき}を{見|み}せてくれる。
examples.english: This garden offers beautiful scenery throughout all four seasons.

notes:
USAGE NOTES:
{春夏秋冬|しゅんかしゅうとう} is a four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) listing the seasons in order: {春|はる} (spring), {夏|なつ} (summer), {秋|あき} (autumn), {冬|ふゆ} (winter). The on'yomi reading gives it a literary, elevated tone.

This expression is often used in contexts emphasizing the beauty and distinctness of Japan's seasonal changes, a recurring theme in Japanese culture.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {春夏秋冬|しゅんかしゅうとう}を{通|つう}じて (throughout all four seasons)
- {春夏秋冬|しゅんかしゅうとう}を{楽|たの}しむ (enjoy all four seasons)
- {春夏秋冬|しゅんかしゅうとう}の{移|うつ}り{変|か}わり (the changing of the seasons)

The expression {四季|しき} (four seasons) is the more common everyday synonym. {春夏秋冬|しゅんかしゅうとう} sounds more poetic and is preferred in literary, travel, and cultural contexts.
